meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_96_packages.json (just created), all reference===96 edges from torahData.js (zero found), and the full source text torah_96.txt (15 lines). Searched for explicit bechina language (הַיְנוּ, כְּלוֹמַר, בְּחִינַת, הוּא בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא) in the source text. Cross-checked every concept named in the source text against the seven reconstructed bechina pairs. The source text has two distinct sections: (A) the explanatory body (lines 2-7) which is predominantly eitza/causal; (B) the verse-interpretation (lines 9-15) which is bechina-dense. All seven bechina pairs from section B were captured in the packages. Section A was examined for any additional bechina-language statements.

additions.source_quote: מֵעֵת הַשְּׁבִירָה נָפְלוּ הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת מִכָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת... נוֹפֵל לוֹ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה מֵעֵין אוֹתָהּ מִדָּה
additions.justification: The source text explains that the machshava zara is ontologically a 'ninotzot' (fallen spark) from the shevirah (breaking of vessels). The phrase 'מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה מֵעֵין אוֹתָהּ מִדָּה' (a foreign thought that is 'of the same quality/type' as that midda) uses 'מֵעֵין' — which means 'of the same kind as', functioning semantically like a weak bechina equivalence. The machshava zara IS a fallen version of the ninotzot from that midda. This implicit bechina (נִיצוֹצוֹת ↔ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה) grounds the entire Torah's cosmological premise. The ninotzot share the essential nature of the machshava zara — they are the same spiritual substance, just one is 'fallen' (the machshava zara that disrupts prayer) and one is 'original' (the spark awaiting elevation). However, the language is not the explicit 'הַיְנוּ' or 'בְּחִינַת' form used in the verse-interpretation section. It is a strong implicit bechina candidate that would logically belong in Package 1.
additions.explicitness_level: implicit — uses 'מֵעֵין' (of the same quality as) rather than explicit 'הַיְנוּ' language

additions.source_quote: וְהַצַּדִּיק צָרִיךְ לֵידַע מֵאֵיזֶה מִדָּה וּמֵאֵיזֶה עוֹלָם הִיא זֹאת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה
additions.justification: The text treats מִדָּה (divine attribute/quality) and עוֹלָם (spiritual world/realm) as near-synonymous structures: the tzaddik must know 'from which midda and from which olam' the machshava zara came, in order to know 'with what to elevate it to that olam and to that midda.' The phrase pairs them interchangeably, implying they are different names for the same structural reality (the level/quality from which the spark fell). This implicit bechina (מִדָּה ↔ עוֹלָם) extends the מַדְרֵגָה node already in Package 2 — all three terms (מדה, עולם, מדרגה) describe the same structural concept: the spiritual station/level that is both the origin of the machshava zara and the destination of its elevation. Suggested package is 2 because this is the tzaddik's navigational knowledge (a positive spiritual faculty), not part of the evil force cluster.
additions.explicitness_level: implicit — both terms used interchangeably in the same syntactic position ('מֵאֵיזֶה מִדָּה וּמֵאֵיזֶה עוֹלָם'), suggesting they are equivalent designators for the same spiritual structure

additions.source_quote: וְצָרִיךְ לֵידַע בַּמֶּה לְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ לְאוֹתוֹ עוֹלָם וּלְאוֹתוֹ הַמִּדָּה שֶׁהוּא עַתָּה בָּהּ
additions.justification: The text speaks of the tzaddik's need to 'elevate it to that olam and to that midda that he is NOW IN' — meaning the midda is also the current madrega (spiritual level) of the tzaddik himself. The midda he is currently in IS his madrega. This is a bechina equivalence: מִדָּה (in the sense of divine quality/attribute) ↔ מַדְרֵגָה (spiritual level), since both describe the tzaddik's current spiritual station. This addition would connect מִדָּה into the מַדְרֵגָה node already in Package 2, extending the three-node level-structure within that package.
additions.explicitness_level: implicit — the text uses both terms to describe the tzaddik's 'current level', equating them through context

additions.source_quote: כִּי כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ מַחֲלֹקֶת עַל אֵיזֶה צַדִּיק, נוֹפֵל מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה מֵעֵין אוֹתָהּ מַחֲלֹקֶת לְצַדִּיק אַחֵר
additions.justification: The body of the teaching (line 7) explicitly states: 'when there is machloket on a certain tzaddik, a machshava zara of the same quality (מֵעֵין) as that machloket falls on another tzaddik.' This means the machshava zara IS 'like' the machloket — they share the same essential spiritual substance. The phrase 'מֵעֵין אוֹתָהּ מַחֲלֹקֶת' (of the same quality as that conflict) is a bechina statement: the machshava zara and the machloket are the same spiritual reality appearing at different levels (inner vs. outer, subjective vs. social). This inner-outer equivalence is the theological heart of the Torah — it explains WHY the tzaddik gets the machshava zara (because of external machloket). This confirms and strengthens the existing Package 1 grouping, adding a narrative-body bechina to the verse-interpretation bechinat already captured. This addition is already implicitly represented in Package 1 (both nodes are there), but the direct equivalence from the body text is noted here as a gap in explicit dataset representation.
additions.explicitness_level: strong implicit — 'מֵעֵין אוֹתָהּ מַחֲלֹקֶת' declares the machshava zara to be of the SAME ESSENCE as the machloket; equivalent to 'הַיְנוּ' in force

additions.source_quote: אַף־עַל־פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה אוֹתָהּ, מְשַׁבֵּר בְּכֹחַ הָרָצוֹן כָּל בַּעֲלֵי הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת
additions.justification: The teaching says that even when the tzaddik cannot elevate the machshava zara, he 'breaks [all the baalei machloket] with the power of the will (כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן).' The 'כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן' is explicitly equated with the חֹרֵק שִׁנַּיִם in the verse interpretation ('חֹרֵק שִׁנַּיִם – הַיְנוּ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ'). But the body text adds the intensified phrase 'כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן' (the power/force of the will) as a distinct name for this faculty. This is a bechina pair within Package 2: כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן ↔ רָצוֹן לְהַעֲלוֹת. Both name the same positive spiritual force of the tzaddik. This addition would enrich the existing Package 2 node 'רָצוֹן לְהַעֲלוֹת' by adding 'כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן' as a connected bechina synonym.
additions.explicitness_level: strong implicit — both terms name the same spiritual act (the tzaddik's will to elevate/break the machloket); 'כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן' in the body and 'שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ' in the verse interpretation are descriptions of the same bechina

source_text_bechina_scan.explicit_bechina_phrases_detail: All 7 explicit bechina statements use the marker 'הַיְנוּ' (i.e., meaning, that is) or 'כְּלוֹמַר' (meaning, in other words) in the verse-interpretation section (lines 9-15). These are: (1) זֹמֵם רָשָׁע – הַיְנוּ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה; (2) וְחֹרֵק עָלָיו שִׁנָּיו – הַיְנוּ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ; (3) כִּי יָבֹא יוֹמוֹ – הַיְנוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא בָּא לְמַדְרֵגַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה; (4) חֶרֶב – לְשׁוֹן מִלְחָמָה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר מַחֲלֹקֶת; (5) חַרְבָּם – הַיְנוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת; (6) תָּבוֹא בְלִבָּם – הַיְנוּ בְּלֵב צַדִּיק זֶה; (7) וְקַשְּׁתוֹתָם תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה – כְּלוֹמַר, הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת הַנַּ"ל.
source_text_bechina_scan.implicit_bechina_candidates_detail: Five implicit bechina candidates were identified using 'מֵעֵין' (of the same quality/type) and contextual equivalence: (1) נִיצוֹצוֹת ↔ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה (same spiritual substance at different states); (2) מִדָּה ↔ עוֹלָם (interchangeable terms for spiritual levels); (3) מִדָּה ↔ מַדְרֵגָה (the tzaddik's midda = his madrega); (4) מַחֲלֹקֶת ↔ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה (inner-outer equivalence declared in body text); (5) כֹּחַ הָרָצוֹן ↔ רָצוֹן לְהַעֲלוֹת (same faculty, two names).

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_analysis: Torah #96 has a clear good/evil mirror structure: Package 1 (evil) = the external and internal forces of disruption (machshava zara / machloket / sword / bow) versus Package 2 (good) = the tzaddik's inner spiritual capacities (heart, will, spiritual level). The evil mirror is unusually explicit because the entire Torah is built on a verse-by-verse decoding: each verse-phrase is identified as either the evil force (Package 1) or the tzaddik's response (Package 2). The evil cluster (sword, bow, wicked plotter) mirrors the good cluster (heart, will, day-that-comes) in perfect structural balance across the verse.
analysis_notes.teaching_structure_summary: Torah #96 argues: The machshava zara during prayer is NOT accidental — it is a fallen spark (ninotzot) from the tzaddik's own spiritual level, OR it is the spiritual manifestation of external machloket (controversy) against a different tzaddik. The tzaddik's response (wanting to elevate it) breaks the machloket even without success. This is the eitza flow: machloket → machshava zara → enters tzaddik's lev → tzaddik's ratzon to elevate → breaks baalei machloket. The two packages (evil force / tzaddik's world) are the two sides of this battle, connected by eitza (the evil force enters the good vessel; the good response breaks the evil).
